decisions.reason: It builds on the firm's advisory and partnership capabilities and the firm's own R&D supports learning, though as a startup program it is less central than the core machinery business.

Despite some link to the recycling business and in-house R&D, a bio-based bitumen binder sits furthest from the firm's core machinery and plant know-how, so absorptive capacity for improving and commercialising it is weaker.

An infectious waste decontamination plant is close to the firm's existing waste-treatment systems, and with strong technical capabilities and R&D the firm is well placed to interpret early market feedback and improve it.

A mobile mechanical recycling plant is highly aligned with the firm's established modular recycling technology, decentralized model, and manufacturing know-how, so it is the strongest candidate to remain on the market.
